name: Querétaro
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Querétaro: aerospace and automotive supplier diligence, industrial real estate and mercantile court support.
hero_lede: Querétaro is one of Mexico's leading manufacturing and investment centres, with aerospace, automotive, electronics and data centre clusters on the corridor north of Mexico City. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for Querétaro matters, coordinating qualified Mexican professionals and counsel where local work is required.
intro: Santiago de Querétaro is the capital of the state of Querétaro, about 200 kilometres north of Mexico City and within three hours of Guadalajara and León. Over the last two decades it has become one of Mexico's most important industrial centres. Aerospace arrived with ITP Aero in 1998 and Bombardier and Safran in 2006, and the cluster now numbers more than 60 companies. General Motors, Scania, Continental and over 100 tier-one suppliers anchor the automotive sector, while Samsung, Siemens and Bosch lead electrical and electronics manufacturing. Google, Microsoft, Amazon and Equinix have made the area a data centre hub. Industry contributed about 42 percent of state GDP at the end of 2022.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Querétaro because foreign manufacturers, investors and lenders there rely on networks of Mexican suppliers, contractors, landowners and service providers that are growing quickly. Relocation of production closer to the United States has brought new projects and new partners, and roughly three-quarters of the state's exports go to the US under the USMCA framework. That growth creates exposures to supplier fraud, conflicts of interest in procurement, disputes over industrial land and construction, and questions about the ownership of local partners. Data centre and power projects add permitting and land questions, and aerospace work brings export control and quality obligations that extend to the supply chain.

matters.title: Aerospace supply chain diligence
matters.text: Querétaro's aerospace cluster depends on machining, composites and maintenance suppliers that must meet strict quality and export control requirements. We research supplier ownership, related companies, litigation and links to restricted parties, helping prime contractors and investors document diligence across a growing local supply base.

matters.title: Automotive supplier and distributor checks
matters.text: Tier-one and tier-two automotive suppliers around Querétaro often work through family groups and affiliated companies. We map shareholders and representatives from commercial registry filings, review mercantile litigation and media coverage, and look for conflicts of interest with purchasing staff before contracts or acquisitions.

matters.title: Industrial land and construction disputes
matters.text: Rapid expansion of industrial parks and data centre campuses brings disputes over land title, ejido origins, permits and construction contracts. We support counsel with research on landowners, developers and contractors, with local professionals retrieving property registry and municipal records where required.

matters.title: Procurement fraud and conflicts of interest
matters.text: Plants in Querétaro buy services, logistics and materials from local vendors, creating room for kickbacks and undisclosed relationships. Working with the client's counsel, we research suspect vendors and their connections to employees through lawful sources, scoped to Mexican labour and data protection rules.

matters.title: Mercantile litigation and asset research
matters.text: Commercial claims involving Querétaro companies are heard in the state's oral mercantile courts or in federal courts. We support counsel with corporate histories, witness backgrounds and identification of companies, property and business interests relevant to enforcement in Querétaro and elsewhere in Mexico.

local_context.title: State courts in Querétaro
local_context.text: The Judicial Branch of the State of Querétaro is organised in six judicial districts, with the Querétaro district holding the largest concentration of courts. As of 2026 that district has nine civil courts and two courts specialised in oral mercantile proceedings, alongside family and criminal courts. Appeals go to the Superior Court of Justice, whose two civil chambers hear civil and commercial appeals, and the judiciary also runs a Centre for Alternative Justice offering mediation and conciliation.

local_context.title: Federal courts and jurisdiction
local_context.text: Mexican commercial law is federal, and many mercantile claims can be brought either in state courts or in federal district courts, with amparo proceedings challenging court and administrative acts heard by the federal judiciary. Federal courts also sit in Querétaro. Counsel will advise on the forum, and our research is shaped around the procedural route chosen, including the documentary evidence each court expects.

local_context.title: Industrial parks and investment bodies
local_context.text: Querétaro has more than 30 active industrial parks, and investment is promoted by the state government's economic development office, which reported 53 projects worth MX$30 billion in 2025. The Aerocluster Querétaro brings together aerospace companies, and the Aeronautical University of Querétaro trains technicians and engineers for the sector. Park operators, developers and cluster bodies are useful starting points when identifying the companies involved in a local supply chain.

local_context.title: Registries for Querétaro businesses
local_context.text: Commercial companies are recorded in the Public Registry of Commerce through the federal SIGER system, while real property is recorded in the state's public property registry, which is administered locally. Research on a Querétaro company therefore combines federal commercial filings, notarial deeds where available through counsel, and state property and court records, with retrieval of certified documents usually carried out in person.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Querétaro and works on Querétaro matters from Nashville. We first agree the purpose with the client and its counsel, whether supplier onboarding in aerospace or automotive, an industrial land or construction dispute, an internal procurement review, an acquisition or a mercantile claim, and scope the research to it. Sources include commercial registry filings, state property and court records, federal court information, Mexican business press and records in the United States and other countries where parties operate. Personal data is handled under Mexico's federal private-sector data protection law. Any local enquiries, record retrieval or site visits are carried out by qualified Mexican professionals under Mexican counsel's guidance.

faqs.q: Do you have an office in Querétaro?
faqs.a: No. TDSC works from Nashville and has no office, staff or address in Mexico. When an engagement needs records retrieved in Querétaro, interviews or a site visit to a plant or property, we coordinate qualified Mexican professionals and work with Mexican counsel, who confirms what each activity requires before it begins.

faqs.q: Where are commercial disputes heard in Querétaro?
faqs.a: Many commercial claims are heard in the Querétaro judicial district's courts specialised in oral mercantile proceedings, with appeals to the civil chambers of the state Superior Court of Justice. Some claims proceed in federal courts instead. Counsel decides the forum, and we tailor background and asset research to its procedures and evidence requirements.

faqs.q: How do you assess an aerospace supplier in Querétaro?
faqs.a: We identify the supplier's shareholders, representatives and related companies from commercial registry filings, review litigation, regulatory and media records, and screen principals and affiliates against restricted-party lists. We also look at foreign parent companies and customers where public information allows, so that quality and export control assessments rest on a clear picture of ownership.

faqs.q: Can you research industrial land before a purchase or lease?
faqs.a: Yes, alongside the client's notary and counsel, who handle title review. We research the landowner, developer and their related companies, look for litigation, agrarian or permitting disputes and media coverage, and arrange for local professionals to retrieve property registry and municipal records where needed. The results help identify risks before commitments are made.

faqs.q: Can you investigate suspected vendor fraud at a Querétaro plant?
faqs.a: We support internal investigations led by the client's counsel. We research the suspect vendors, their owners and addresses, and possible links to employees through lawful public sources, and help organise the findings for counsel. Interviews and any review of employee data are scoped with Mexican counsel to respect labour and data protection rules.
